source_refs.note: Exercise 3.3, Question 10: book p. 89-90, 24 questions (integration by parts); answer key p. 301 (printed under 'Exercise 3.5')

blocks.explanation:
Yahan \(e^{x^2}\) ke saath ek bracket hai. Kitab ka Note yaad kijiye: \(\int e^{g(x)}[f(x)g'(x) + f'(x)]\,dx = e^{g(x)}f(x) + c\).
\(g(x) = x^2\) lein to \(g'(x) = 2x\). Agar \(f(x) = x^2\) ho to \(fg' + f' = 2x^3 + 2x\), bilkul hamara bracket!
Is liye jawab \(x^2e^{x^2}\) hona chahiye. Lekin hum ise parts se bhi saabit karenge taa ke wajah samajh aaye.
Plan: integral ko torein, \(2x^3e^{x^2} = x^2 \cdot 2xe^{x^2}\) par parts lagayein; bacha hua integral cancel ho jayega.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int (2x^3 + 2x)e^{x^2}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: integral torenge; \(\int x^2\cdot 2xe^{x^2}\,dx\) mein \(x^2\) first aur \(2xe^{x^2}\) second (jis ka integral \(e^{x^2}\) hai).

Torein
\[= \int x^2\cdot 2xe^{x^2}\,dx + \int 2xe^{x^2}\,dx\]
Kyun: \(2x^3 = x^2\cdot 2x\) likha, kyunke \(2xe^{x^2}\) ka integral humein aata hai: \(\frac{d}{dx}e^{x^2} = 2xe^{x^2}\).

Pehle integral par parts
\[\int x^2\cdot 2xe^{x^2}\,dx = x^2e^{x^2} - \int e^{x^2}\cdot 2x\,dx\]
Kyun: second function \(2xe^{x^2}\) ka integral \(e^{x^2}\) (chain rule ka ulta), first \(x^2\) ka derivative \(2x\).
Dhyan dein: \(e^{x^2}\) ko akela integrate karne ki koshish na karein; woh kisi aam function mein nahi nikalta. \(2x\) saath ho tabhi aasaan hai.

Integrals cancel
\[= x^2e^{x^2} - \int 2xe^{x^2}\,dx + \int 2xe^{x^2}\,dx\]
\[= x^2e^{x^2} + c\]
Kyun: ek hi integral ek dafa minus aur ek dafa plus ke saath; dono khatam. Yahi Note ka jawab \(e^{g}f = e^{x^2}x^2\) hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^2e^{x^2}) = 2xe^{x^2} + x^2\cdot 2xe^{x^2}\]
\[= (2x^3 + 2x)e^{x^2}\]
Kyun: product rule aur chain rule; bilkul integrand.
